MIDTERM PRESENTATION

StyleVector: Personalized Text Generation
via Contrastive Activation Steering

A reproduction study of Zhang et al. (ACL 2025), with an extension toward multi-component, norm-preserving steering.

Slok Tulsyan · 12342080 Machine Learning Course Project
01 · MOTIVATION

LLMs write in one voice. People don't.

Personalized generation needs a user's writing style — existing approaches pay a steep price for it.

RAG

Retrieves past examples at inference time. Latency grows with history size; content and style stay entangled.

PEFT

Trains a per-user adapter. Needs storage and training time for every single user.

StyleVector

Encodes style as one vector per user. No retrieval, no training, no per-user parameters.

02 · THE PAPER'S CORE IDEA

Style is a direction in activation space

Contrast a user's authentic writing against a style-agnostic version of the same content — the difference, averaged over their history, is their style vector.

Add that vector back into the model's hidden state during generation, and the model writes like them — no retraining required.

03 · METHOD

Three stages, four equations

STAGE 1
Generate a style-agnostic response for each historical input
→
STAGE 2
Contrast activations: authentic vs. style-agnostic, averaged
→
STAGE 3
Add the resulting vector during generation, at one layer
Eq. 4 — style-agnostic response
ŷᵢ = M_g(xᵢ)
Eq. 5 — contrastive activations
a_p,ᵢ = h_ℓ(xᵢ ⊕ yᵢ)   a_n,ᵢ = h_ℓ(xᵢ ⊕ ŷᵢ)
Eq. 7 — Mean Difference style vector
sᵘ_ℓ = (1/|Pᵤ|) Σᵢ (a_p,ᵢ − a_n,ᵢ)
Eq. 11 — steered generation
h'_ℓ(x)ₜ = h_ℓ(x)ₜ + α · sᵘ_ℓ
04 · OUR REPRODUCTION

Matching the paper, disclosing where we couldn't

MATCHES THE PAPER

  • Model: LLaMA-2-7B-chat
  • Exact prompts (Appendix E)
  • Greedy decoding
  • Validation-tuned layer & α, per task

DISCLOSED DEVIATIONS

  • 4-bit quantization, not 8-bit — 12GB VRAM on our GPU
  • Public dev split, not the hidden test set
  • History capped for compute feasibility
05 · METHODOLOGICAL RIGOR

A double-wrapped prompt was quietly hurting our baseline

LaMP's own input field is already the fully-rendered instruction. Re-applying our prompt template wrapped it a second time.

− prompt = prompt_fn(u["query_input"]) # double-wraps an already-rendered prompt
+ prompt = u["query_input"] # use LaMP's rendered prompt as-is

Caught by comparing a single live generation against its own aggregate benchmark score — they didn't match. Fixed, and the full evaluation was re-run before these results.

07 · KEY FINDING

Reproduction fidelity tracks the paper's own effect size

Tasks where the paper reports a large improvement (Tweet Paraphrasing) reproduce closely, in both direction and magnitude.

Tasks with the smallest reported effect (News Headline Generation) are the most sensitive to implementation differences — exactly what you'd expect statistically from a fragile, small effect.

This is not a failure to reproduce — it's a quantified, testable pattern discovered by comparing across tasks, not just within one.

09 · HONEST LIMITATIONS

What we're not claiming

  • Absolute scores are not a byte-for-byte match to the paper — different model scale, sample, and no released source code to compare against.
  • Single-reference ROUGE-L/METEOR penalize equally valid paraphrases on Tweet Paraphrasing — a known metric limitation, not a method failure.
  • Evaluated on the public dev split; the paper's exact test conditions are not independently verifiable without their code.
10 · TOWARD THE END-TERM

Our proposed extension

A single Mean Difference vector may conflate multiple, independent stylistic dimensions — the paper's own stated limitation.

Multi-component style vectors

Top-k PCA over contrastive differences, instead of a single mean direction.

Norm-preserving steering

Rescale after steering to prevent the activation-magnitude blowup the paper's own Fig. 3 shows at high α.

Thank you

Questions welcome — including a live re-run of the demo on any prompt you'd like to try.
